With the articulation of ‘Make in India’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ vision, the manufacturing of all kinds of d efence equipment in the country has got tremendous impetus. However, self-reliance in the defence secto r has two dimensions. First is the acquisition of new platforms and equipment that are indigenous. The sec ond is the indigenous manufacture and repair of systems, components, spares and subassemblies to sustai n the in-service platforms of foreign origin. Presently, repair and sustenance of foreign origin platforms ent ails considerable outgo of forex as well as continued dependency on foreign Original Equipment Manufactu rers (OEMs) for spares, maintenance, repairs and overhauls. This impacts our strategic autonomy and defe nce preparedness. Achieving Atmanirbharta or self-reliance in both dimensions is a strategic imperative a nd should be seen as a national mission. 10.2.2 Atmanirbhar Bharat, in the context of MoD, hence, refers t o achievement of self-reliance in manufacturing and production of defence items, ammunition, spares, etc. as well as services within the country. The objective of self-reliance in defence is sought to be achieved thr ough development of Defence items, spare parts etc. needed by the defence forces for sustenance and to ensure the availability of infrastructure required for manufacture and production of such goods/services wi thin the country. 10.2.3 Rule 153 (iii) of General Financial Rules provides that the Central Government ma y, by notification, provide for mandatory procurement of any goods or services from any category of (204) CHAPTER 10 DPM - 2025 bidders, or provide for preference to bidders on the grounds of promotion of locall y manufactured goods or locally provided services. Guidelines have further been laid down by Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade vide Procurement Preference to Make in India (MII policy) orde r OM no. P-45021/2/2017-PP (BE-II)-part (4)vol-II dt 19th July 2024 and its amendments from time to time i n Indian defence revenue procurement under the Defence Procurement Manual (DPM) 2025, the OE M Tec hnical Brochure and the Technical Compliance Matrix (Statement of Technical Compliance - STC) are crucia l components submitted during the Technical Evaluation process. (x) Brochure and technical compliance. The product literature or technical brochure provided by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) or ve ndor serves as the baseline technical proof during evaluation. • Authenticity & Completeness: Must be an official, published document from the manufacturer (digital or printed) clearly outlining specifications, performance parameters, and operational capabilities. • Traceability: Every claim made in the vendor's technical bid must correlate directly with features docum ented in the brochure. • Language: Must be provided in English or accompanied by an official, notarized English translation. (xi) Non-neighbouring country component certificate. Certification regarding the country of origin and component breakdown—commonly referred to as the Certificate of Country of Origin or Indigenous Content (IC) / Local Content Certificate—plays a critical role i n payment processing, quality assurance, and compliance with Make in India / Aatmanirbhar Bharat guideli

nes. i. Primary Purpose of the Certificate • Verification of Origin: Serves as legal proof declaring the country where the supplied store, equipment, s ub-assembly, or software was manufactured, processed, or assembled. • Compliance with Import Regulations: Restricts unauthorized routing of equipment from embargoed or re stricted foreign sources. • Local Content Enforcement: Verifies whether a bid qualifies under Public Procurement (Preference to Mak e in India) orders by establishing the exact percentage of indigenous components versus imported sub-ass emblies. ii. Standard Provisions & Requirements in DPM 2025 a. Submission Stage & Supporting Documents The Certificate of Country of Origin / Component Breakdown is submitted by the vendor alongside key deli very and bill processing documents, which typically include: 1. Certificate of Country of Origin issued by the OEM or an authorized Chamber of Commerce/Government agency. 2. OEM Certificate of Quality and Current Manufacture. 3. Certificate of Conformity & Acceptance Test (PDI/JDI) signed by Quality Assurance (QA) representatives. 4. Self-Declaration of Indigenous / Local Content specifying the breakdown of local vs. imported raw mater ials, assemblies, and components. b. Component & Origin Declarations 1. Direct Import Contracts: Requires an official Chamber of Commerce certificate from the origin country v erifying that the items were manufactured in the declared nation. 2. Domestic Suppliers offering Foreign Equipment/Components: Must explicitly declare the imported comp onents, their country of origin, and custom duty clearance receipts (Bill of Entry) to ensure transparency. 3. Indigenous Equipment: Bidders claiming preference or exemption under indigenization chapters must s ubmit a certified self-declaration showing the break-up of domestic value addition (cost of domestic materi als, local labour, and overheads vs. foreign imported components). Foreign Procurement Restrictions: DPM 2025 strictly regulates foreign purchases by requiring explicit au thorization for import items, ensuring domestic alternatives are prioritized where available. 2.
